messages.author: d54aba6af40f8c5e
messages.subject: RR from Bayesian logistic model
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to estimate the Relative Risk (RR) from a logistic model. In the frequentist realm one often instead fits a Poisson model to binary data and then then fixes up the obvious model misspecification using a sandwich estimator. However, with Bayesian MCMC one can directly estimate the RR from a logistic model. (See: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/259486968_Using_Bayesian_Logistic_Regression_to_Estimate_the_Risk_or_Prevalence_Ratio)

I can successfully implement the approach in the above cited paper via INLA, however I end up creating a dummy dataset of triple the size of the original. This approach works, but I wonder if there is a more efficient way to do this.

Thanks,

John
------------------------------------------------------------

library(tidyverse)
library(MASS)

## Here's the paper
### https://www.researchgate.net/publication/259486968_Using_Bayesian_Logistic_Regression_to_Estimate_the_Risk_or_Prevalence_Ratio

##########################
### Simulate some data ###
##########################
                                       
set.seed(123)
n <- 1000
x1 <- rnorm(n)
x2 <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)
eta <- 0.5 + 0.5 * x1 - 1.5 * x2
y <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(eta))

###########################################
### Fit robust Poisson regression model ###
###########################################

library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)
model <- glm(y ~ 1 + x1 + x2, family = poisson(link = "log"))
summary(model)
ct <- coeftest(model,vcov=sandwich)

ct.est <- ct["x2","Estimate"]
ct.error <- ct["x2","Std. Error"]
ct.ci <- exp(ct.est + c(-1,1) * 1.96 * ct.error)

###################################
### Fit Bayesian logistic model ###
###################################

library(brms)

dat <- tibble(y,x1,x2)
m.bayes <- brm(
    y ~ x1 + x2,
    family = bernoulli(),
    data=dat
)
mat <- as_tibble(m.bayes)

dat.0 <- dat %>%
    mutate(x2=0)
dat.1 <- dat %>%
    mutate(x2=1)
dat.pred <- rbind(dat.0,dat.1)

pl <- posterior_linpred(m.bayes,newdata=dat.pred)

mf <- function(vec.org) {
    vec <- plogis(vec.org)
    bot <- mean(vec[1:n])
    top <- mean(vec[n+1:n])
    res <- top / bot
}
rr <- apply(pl,1,mf)
median(rr)
quantile(rr,probs=c(0.5,0.025,0.975))

############
### INLA ###
############

library(INLA)

dat.pred.inla <- dat.pred %>%
    mutate(y = NA)
dat.inla <- rbind(dat,dat.pred.inla)

m.inla <- inla(
    y ~ x1 + x2,
    family = "binomial",
    control.compute=list(config=TRUE),
    control.predictor=list(link=1),
    data=dat.inla
)

get.samp <- function(mod,M=1000,seed=1,num.threads="1:1") {
    samp <- inla.posterior.sample(M,mod,seed=seed,num.threads=num.threads)
    latents <- t(sapply(samp,function(x) x$latent[,1]))
}
samp <- get.samp(m.inla,M=10000)
pl.inla <- cbind(samp[,n + 1:n],samp[,2*n+1:n])
rr.inla <- apply(pl.inla,1,mf)
quantile(rr.inla,probs=c(0.5,0.025,0.975))

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] RR from Bayesian logistic model
parts:
I think what you do is fine. the cost of adding more data is linear in number of
data

maybe you do not need to set seed and num.threads as its runs better without:
